newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank sees earnings rising in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank sees earnings rising in 1996.

text.p: Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank AG, Germany's fifth-largest listed bank, said on Tuesday its operating profit before risk provisions rose moderately in the first four months of 1997 and exceeded the 1.5 percent growth rate recorded in the first quarter.

The bank also predicted full-year 1997 earnings would exceed 1996. Chief executive Eberhard Martini said in a speech prepared for the annual shareholders meeting that the bank had made progress in reducing its exposure to problem loans.
Martini said that given the sluggish economy and high corporate insolvencies there was no reason to sound the all-clear regarding banks' risk exposure.
The real estate market in particular, where Hypo-Bank has a high market share, was showing no signs of an upturn, he added.
But he added: "We are confident that we have made a significant step forward in overcoming our problem loan cases, as is being signalled by falling risk quotas in most loan areas."
